description:
## Finding

Seven create-object handler call sites in `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/`
pass `Id::from("placeholder")` as the synthetic `id` field of the
constructed object, expecting the backend to overwrite it with the
real assigned id during `create_object`. The rustdoc on
`ChatBackend::create_object` (`backend.rs:296-307`) is **silent**
about this sentinel contract.

## Verified call sites (7)

```
crate-jmap-chat-server/src/ban.rs:161:        Id::from("placeholder"),
crate-jmap-chat-server/src/chat.rs:277:       Id::from("placeholder"),
crate-jmap-chat-server/src/emoji.rs:403:      Id::from("placeholder"),
crate-jmap-chat-server/src/invite.rs:220:     Id::from("placeholder"),
crate-jmap-chat-server/src/message.rs:450:    Id::from("placeholder"),
crate-jmap-chat-server/src/position.rs:161:   ReadPosition::new(Id::from("placeholder"), chat_id);
crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:829:      Id::from("placeholder"),
```

## The contract rustdoc

`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:296-307` verbatim:

```
/// Create a new object.
///
/// Returns `(assigned_id, created_object)` on success. `create_id` is the
/// client-side creation id used in the `/set` request.
fn create_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
    &self,
    caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
    account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    create_id: &str,
    obj: O,
) -> impl Future<...> + Send;
```

Two paragraphs of rustdoc, neither mentions that `obj.id` is a
magic `"placeholder"` string the backend MUST overwrite.

## What goes wrong for a third-party implementer

A custom `ChatBackend` impl that trusts the `obj` argument's `id`
field — natural for an implementer reading the rustdoc — will
persist `"placeholder"` as the wire-format id of every newly-
created Space, Chat, Message, SpaceInvite, SpaceBan, CustomEmoji,
and ReadPosition. The kit's smoke tests do not catch this
because `MemoryBackend` correctly overwrites (`memory.rs` per-type
`create_object` impls all derive a fresh id and discard `obj.id`).

The failure mode is silent: no compile error, no panic, no test
fixture exercises the input `id` field, and the resulting wire
output (`Space { id: "placeholder", ... }`) is structurally valid
JMAP.

## Comparison to mail-server (canonical-template lens)

Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates" and the
chat-server AGENTS.md sibling banner, jmap-mail-server is the
canonical extension-server template. Mail-server's `create_object`
doc at `crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:64-87` carries an
explicit "Sentinel fields the backend MUST replace" section.
Chat-server lacks this paragraph.

This is chat-server **drift below the canonical** — fix is
chat-server-local to mirror the canonical pattern (not a
propagation epic to mail-server).

## Recommendation

Add a "Sentinel fields the backend MUST replace" section to
`ChatBackend::create_object`'s doc, mirroring mail-server's
shape. Enumerate `id` (`"placeholder"`) and any other
fields the per-type handlers pre-set.

A type-system fix (e.g. an `IdOrPlaceholder` newtype enum, or
making `id` an `Option<Id>` in the `O` value passed to
`create_object`) would close the footgun structurally but
imposes ergonomic cost on every handler and may not pay back the
churn for a pre-1.0 crate. Doc fix is the minimum viable.

## Engineering basis

Verified by:
1. Grep `Id::from("placeholder")` across `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/`
   — 7 hits at 7 distinct files, all in handler create paths.
2. Direct read of `backend.rs:296-307` — rustdoc is 2 lines and says
   nothing about the sentinel.
3. Mail-server cross-walk: `crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:64-87`
   has the analogous doc paragraph.

## Cross-reference

This is the chat-server arm of the N1 pattern noted in
JMAP-x2gd.67's "New patterns discovered in mail-server during
the cross-walk" section. JMAP-x2gd.67 marked N1 as
"mail-server-LOCAL" with the caveat "spot-check: chat-server's
create_object does NOT appear to have N1's placeholder-
sentinel-input contract, but I read the doc once not deeply.
Could be wrong." This finding closes that uncertainty: chat-server
DOES have the pattern, in 7 sites, and its docstring is worse
than mail-server's.
title: API contract: ChatBackend::create_object doc is silent on the placeholder Id::from("placeholder") sentinel contract used in 7 handler call sites
